Well… I’m here because there’s been a situation at work, and it’s been going on for months now. I’m an interpreter and translator, so a lot of my work depends on project files, translation memories, timestamps, version histories—things most people don’t look at closely, but I do, because quality control depends on it.

It’s arranged so it looks clean.

I did raise it with IT, and they keep saying the audit trail is clean, that there’s no evidence of tampering. But that doesn’t really settle it for me, because the record can be arranged. I know how these systems work enough to know that what shows up afterward isn’t always the full story. And the way the blame keeps landing in my direction… it’s too consistent to be accidental.

So I guess that’s why I’m here. People are acting like I’m overreacting, but I’m not. I just need someone to actually listen to the whole thing instead of dismissing it because the official log says everything is fine.

I’m… very certain. I know that sounds strong, and I’m not saying I saw his hands on the keyboard changing a file in front of me, but the pattern has been too consistent to explain away.

I’m not sure I’d put it that way, no. Before this work situation, I don’t think I went around assuming people had bad motives. The thing I can actually point to is the work situation, because that’s where the pattern is.\n\nFor months I’ve been seeing these small alterations in the project files—translation memory entries, timestamps, version histories—and it’s always just subtle enough that someone could say, “Oh, that’s normal,” or “You’re reading too much into it.” But then the outcome is that it reflects badly on me, like my quality control failed or I missed something I shouldn’t have missed.\n\nAnd it’s not everyone, but there are certain subcontractors, and one colleague especially, where the same kind of thing keeps happening. IT says the audit trail is clean, but that doesn’t reassure me, because the record itself can be arranged afterward to look clean. That’s part of what makes it so difficult to explain. So outside work, no, I don’t have a separate concern like that. But at work, yes, I do believe they’re deliberately undermining me.\n\nDoctor: If IT showed you clear proof that no one had altered the files, would you believe it?\n\nPatient: I would look at it, of course. I’m not saying I’d refuse to read what IT showed me. But “clear proof” is the difficult part, because every time they’ve said the audit trail is clean, that’s been treated like the end of the discussion, and to me it isn’t.\n\nWith these systems, the record is only showing what it’s been allowed to show. If someone knows what they’re doing, the timestamps and version history can be made to look ordinary. That’s exactly what concerns me — the changes are tiny, in the translation memory or the timing of the files, and then later it somehow lands on me, like I missed a quality-control issue.\n\nSo if IT came in and said, “Look, no one altered anything,” I’d want to know what they checked, who had access, whether subcontractor handoffs were reviewed, whether the colleague I’m concerned about had any opportunity to adjust things before the record was finalized. Because if the whole point is to make it look clean, then a clean audit trail doesn’t really disprove it.\n\nI know that may sound like I’m being stubborn, but after months of seeing the same pattern, I don’t think I could just accept a report at face value and say, “Oh, I must have imagined it.” I’d need something that actually explains why the blame keeps ending up on me in the same way.\n\nDoctor: Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?\n\nPatient: No, I don’t think so. I mean, not in the sense of hearing someone speaking when there’s nobody there. But the timing is pretty clear in my mind: I was given responsibility for that project, and not long after that, these issues started appearing. So yes, if you mean did it begin around a stressful work change, then… yes, around then.\n\nDoctor: How certain are you that your colleague is deliberately altering the files to make you look bad?\n\nPatient: I’m… very certain. Sometimes I go over things a lot, probably too much, especially when I’m trying to work out what happened or why something doesn’t add up. But it still feels like me thinking. It’s not as if a thought suddenly appears and I feel, “That wasn’t mine,” or like someone reached in and took an idea away.\n\nI can get distracted, and I can lose my train of thought if I’m tired or focused on too many details, but that’s different. That feels normal, or at least understandable. I still do the normal things I’ve always done.\n\nDoctor: Before this work problem began, did you generally find it hard to trust other people’s motives?\n\nPatient: I’m not sure I’d put it that way, no. If something didn’t add up, I would ask questions. But I don’t think I was suspicious as a general habit, or that I thought people were secretly against me. No, I don’t think so. I mean, I see the same things other people would see if they looked at the screen or the file history closely enough. It’s not like I’m seeing people in the room who aren’t there, or shapes, or anything like that.
